questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A fire caused by burning ordinary combustible materials such as wood, paper, and cloth is classified as a
questions.explanation: Class A fires involve ordinary combustible materials like wood, paper, and cloth.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A fire caused by flammable liquids such as petrol, oil, and paint is classified as a
questions.explanation: Class B fires involve flammable liquids such as petrol, diesel, and oil, common hazards in an auto workshop.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A fire caused by electrical equipment, such as a short-circuited wire or motor, is classified as a
questions.explanation: Class C fires involve energised electrical equipment, requiring a non-conductive extinguishing agent.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A fire caused by combustible metals, such as magnesium, is classified as a
questions.explanation: Class D fires involve combustible metals and require specialised extinguishing agents, as water can worsen these fires.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A fire extinguisher containing water is generally suitable for use on
questions.explanation: Water extinguishers are effective on Class A fires but are unsafe for electrical fires and can worsen flammable liquid or metal fires.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A fire extinguisher containing carbon dioxide (CO2) is particularly suitable for
options: Class B and Class C fires
questions.explanation: CO2 extinguishers smother the fire by displacing oxygen and, being non-conductive, are safe for use on flammable liquid and electrical fires.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: Protective clothing worn in an auto workshop, such as overalls and safety boots, is primarily intended to
options: protect the worker from injury, burns, and contamination
improve the worker's speed of movement only
reduce the cost of workshop insurance only
questions.explanation: Personal protective equipment (PPE) is worn to shield workshop staff from hazards such as burns, cuts, chemical exposure, and falling objects.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: Safety goggles worn while grinding or drilling metal parts primarily protect the
options: eyes from flying debris and sparks
questions.explanation: Safety goggles shield the eyes from metal fragments, sparks, and dust generated during grinding, drilling, or cutting operations.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The first step generally recommended when treating a minor workshop burn is to
options: cool the affected area with clean, cool running water
rub the burn vigorously to relieve pain
apply oil or grease to the burn immediately
questions.explanation: Cooling a burn promptly with clean running water helps reduce tissue damage and relieve pain before further first-aid treatment.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A tool used to tighten or loosen nuts and bolts by fitting over their hexagonal head is called a
questions.explanation: A spanner (or wrench) is designed to grip and turn nuts and bolts, fitting closely over their hexagonal or square heads.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A tool consisting of a set of interchangeable, hollow cylindrical attachments used with a ratchet handle to turn nuts and bolts is called a
questions.explanation: A socket set provides interchangeable sockets that fit onto a ratchet handle, allowing efficient tightening or loosening of various nut and bolt sizes.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A hand tool with a pointed or flat tip used to turn screws is called a
questions.explanation: A screwdriver is designed with a shaped tip (flat or Phillips) to engage and turn the corresponding screw head.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A gripping hand tool with pivoted jaws, commonly used to hold, bend, or cut wire and small components, is called
questions.explanation: Pliers have pivoted jaws used for gripping, bending, or cutting materials such as wire and small fasteners.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A tool with a sharpened edge, struck with a hammer, used to cut or shape metal is called a
questions.explanation: A chisel has a hardened cutting edge and is struck with a hammer to cut, shape, or remove metal.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A hand tool with a hardened, ridged surface used to smooth or shape metal surfaces by abrasion is called a
questions.explanation: A file has a hardened, ridged surface used to smooth, shape, or remove small amounts of material from metal surfaces.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An instrument used to measure the pressure within a system, such as tyre pressure or fuel pressure, is called a
questions.explanation: A pressure gauge measures the pressure of a fluid or gas within a system, useful for checking tyres, fuel systems, or cooling systems.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An instrument used to measure the compression pressure produced within an engine's cylinders is called a
questions.explanation: A compression tester measures the maximum pressure generated in each cylinder during the compression stroke, helping to diagnose engine condition.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A precision instrument used to measure very small dimensions, such as the diameter of a piston or shaft, to a high degree of accuracy is called a
questions.explanation: A micrometer provides highly precise measurements of small dimensions, essential for checking engine component tolerances.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A tool used to tighten fasteners to a specific, measured rotational force (tightness) is called a
questions.explanation: A torque wrench allows a fastener to be tightened to a precise torque specification, preventing under- or over-tightening.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An electronic diagnostic device connected to a vehicle's onboard computer to read fault codes and system data is called a
questions.explanation: A scan tool interfaces with a vehicle's electronic control systems to retrieve diagnostic trouble codes and live sensor data.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine that burns its fuel internally, within its own cylinders, to produce power is called an
questions.explanation: Internal combustion engines burn fuel directly within their cylinders, unlike external combustion engines, which burn fuel outside the working chamber (such as a steam engine).

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine that burns its fuel outside the cylinder, using the resulting heat to generate power indirectly (such as a steam engine), is called an
questions.explanation: External combustion engines burn fuel outside the main working chamber, transferring heat energy to a separate medium (like steam) to produce power.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine that ignites its air-fuel mixture through the heat of highly compressed air, without a spark plug, is called a
questions.explanation: Diesel engines rely on the heat generated by high compression to ignite the fuel, rather than an electric spark.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine that ignites its air-fuel mixture using a timed electric spark from a spark plug is called a
questions.explanation: Petrol (gasoline) engines use a spark plug to ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture at a precisely timed moment.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine that completes its full operating cycle (intake, compression, power, exhaust) within one revolution of the crankshaft is called a
questions.explanation: A two-stroke engine completes its full cycle in just two piston strokes (one crankshaft revolution), combining some strokes together.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine that completes its full operating cycle over two revolutions of the crankshaft, using four distinct piston strokes, is called a
questions.explanation: A four-stroke engine uses four separate piston strokes (intake, compression, power, exhaust) across two crankshaft revolutions for one complete cycle.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The main structural component of an engine, housing the cylinders in which the pistons move, is called the
questions.explanation: The cylinder block is the main engine casting, containing the cylinder bores within which the pistons reciprocate.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine component fitted on top of the cylinder block, containing the combustion chambers and valve mechanisms, is called the
questions.explanation: The cylinder head seals the top of the cylinders and typically houses the combustion chambers, valves, and, in OHC engines, the camshaft.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine component that moves up and down within the cylinder, transferring the force of combustion to the connecting rod, is called the
questions.explanation: The piston receives the force of combustion and transmits it, via the connecting rod, to the crankshaft as rotational motion.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine component fitted around the piston to seal the gap between the piston and cylinder wall, preventing gas leakage, is called the
questions.explanation: Piston rings seal the combustion chamber against gas leakage and help control oil consumption along the cylinder wall.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The small pin connecting the piston to the connecting rod, allowing the rod to pivot as the piston moves, is called the
questions.explanation: The gudgeon pin links the piston to the connecting rod's small end, allowing the necessary pivoting motion as the piston reciprocates.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine component that transmits the piston's reciprocating motion to the crankshaft is called the
questions.explanation: The connecting rod links the piston (via the gudgeon pin) to the crankshaft, converting reciprocating motion into rotational motion.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine component that converts the reciprocating motion of the pistons into useful rotational motion is called the
questions.explanation: The crankshaft converts the up-and-down (reciprocating) motion of the pistons into the rotational motion used to drive the vehicle's transmission.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The heavy rotating disc attached to the crankshaft, which stores rotational energy to smooth out engine power delivery, is called the
questions.explanation: The flywheel's mass stores rotational energy, smoothing out the pulses of power delivery between combustion strokes.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine component with lobes that open and close the intake and exhaust valves at precisely timed intervals is called the
questions.explanation: The camshaft's lobes push against the valve mechanism to open and close the intake and exhaust valves at the correct points in the engine cycle.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The engine components that open to allow air-fuel mixture into the cylinder, and open again to allow exhaust gases out, are called the
questions.explanation: Valves control the flow of gases into and out of the cylinder, opening and closing in time with the piston's movement and the camshaft's rotation.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine valve arrangement in which the camshaft is located in the cylinder block, operating the valves through pushrods, is called
questions.explanation: In an OHV configuration, the camshaft sits in the cylinder block, and pushrods transmit its motion up to operate valves located in the cylinder head.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine valve arrangement in which the camshaft is located directly in the cylinder head, operating the valves without pushrods, is called
questions.explanation: In an OHC configuration, the camshaft is mounted directly in the cylinder head, allowing more direct and precise valve operation without pushrods.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An engine configuration using two camshafts in the cylinder head, one for intake valves and one for exhaust valves, is called a
questions.explanation: DOHC engines use two separate camshafts in the cylinder head, one dedicated to intake valves and the other to exhaust valves, often improving performance.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The small clearance deliberately left between a valve and its operating mechanism, allowing for thermal expansion, is called
questions.explanation: Valve clearance (lash) is a small gap allowed in the valve train to accommodate thermal expansion, ensuring valves close fully when the engine is hot.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: In a petrol engine's fuel system, the component that draws fuel from the tank and delivers it toward the carburettor or injection system is called the
questions.explanation: The fuel (lift) pump draws fuel from the tank and delivers it under pressure toward the carburettor or fuel injection system.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A device that mixes air and fuel in the correct proportion for combustion in older petrol engines, before electronic fuel injection became standard, is called a
questions.explanation: A carburettor mixes air and fuel mechanically in the correct ratio for combustion, a technology largely superseded by electronic fuel injection in modern vehicles.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: In a carburettor, the circuit responsible for supplying fuel during idling (when the throttle is nearly closed) is called the
questions.explanation: The idle circuit supplies the small, precisely metered amount of fuel needed to keep the engine running smoothly at idle speed.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: In a petrol engine's electronic fuel injection (EFI) system, the component that precisely sprays a metered amount of fuel into the intake manifold or cylinder is called the
questions.explanation: Fuel injectors spray precisely metered fuel directly into the intake manifold or combustion chamber, controlled electronically for accuracy.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: In an electronic fuel injection system, the component that processes sensor data and controls fuel delivery and ignition timing is called the
questions.explanation: The ECU is the central computer that processes data from various sensors to precisely control fuel injection, ignition timing, and other engine functions.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: In a diesel engine's fuel system, the component responsible for delivering fuel at very high pressure to the injectors is called the
questions.explanation: The fuel injection pump generates the very high pressures required to deliver diesel fuel precisely to the injectors for combustion.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: In a diesel engine, the small electrical heating device used to preheat the combustion chamber for easier cold starting is called a
questions.explanation: Glow plugs preheat the combustion chamber in diesel engines, aiding ignition and easier starting, especially in cold conditions.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A modern diesel fuel system technology using a single high-pressure fuel line shared by all injectors, allowing very precise electronic injection control, is called
questions.explanation: Common rail direct injection (CRDI) supplies fuel to all injectors from a shared high-pressure 'rail', enabling precise, electronically controlled injection.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A cooling system that uses air passing over finned engine surfaces, without any liquid coolant, is called
questions.explanation: Air-cooled engines dissipate heat directly to the surrounding air via finned surfaces, rather than circulating a liquid coolant.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A cooling system that circulates a liquid coolant through the engine and a radiator to dissipate heat is called
questions.explanation: Liquid-cooled engines circulate coolant through internal passages and a radiator, transferring engine heat to the coolant and then to the surrounding air.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The cooling system component that dissipates heat from the coolant to the surrounding air, typically located at the front of the vehicle, is called the
questions.explanation: The radiator allows heated coolant to pass through thin tubes and fins, releasing heat to the airflow passing through it.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The cooling system component that circulates coolant through the engine block and radiator is called the
questions.explanation: The water pump circulates coolant continuously through the engine and radiator, maintaining effective heat transfer.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The cooling system component that regulates coolant flow to the radiator based on engine temperature, helping the engine reach and maintain optimal operating temperature, is called the
questions.explanation: The thermostat opens and closes based on coolant temperature, restricting flow to the radiator until the engine reaches its optimal operating temperature.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The cooling system component that draws air through the radiator to enhance heat dissipation, especially at low vehicle speeds, is called the
questions.explanation: The cooling fan draws additional air through the radiator, particularly important at idle or low speeds when natural airflow is insufficient.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A lubrication system that relies on rotating engine components splashing oil onto moving parts is called
questions.explanation: Splash lubrication relies on the motion of rotating parts, such as the crankshaft, to splash oil onto other components needing lubrication.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A lubrication system that uses a pump to force oil under pressure to engine components through internal passages is called
questions.explanation: Pressure lubrication uses an oil pump to actively force oil through internal galleries to critical engine components, ensuring consistent lubrication.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The lubrication system component that circulates engine oil under pressure to moving parts is called the
questions.explanation: The oil pump draws oil from the sump and circulates it under pressure through the engine's oil galleries to lubricate moving parts.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The lubrication system component that removes contaminants and debris from circulating engine oil is called the
questions.explanation: The oil filter traps dirt, metal particles, and other contaminants from the oil before it circulates to the engine's moving parts.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The reservoir located at the bottom of the engine that collects and stores oil for the lubrication system is called the
questions.explanation: The oil pan (sump) collects and stores the engine's oil supply, from which the oil pump draws to circulate lubrication.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) viscosity classification of engine oil, such as '20W-50', indicates the oil's
questions.explanation: SAE viscosity grades describe how an oil's thickness (flow characteristics) behaves across a range of temperatures, important for cold starting and hot running performance.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The American Petroleum Institute (API) service classification of engine oil indicates the oil's
options: quality and suitability for specific engine types and service conditions
questions.explanation: API service classifications rate an oil's quality and performance level, indicating its suitability for particular engine types, ages, and operating conditions.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A traditional ignition system using a mechanical contact breaker and a battery/coil arrangement to generate the spark is called
questions.explanation: Conventional battery/coil ignition uses mechanical contact breaker points and a battery-powered coil to generate the timed spark for combustion.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An ignition system that generates its own electrical spark without relying on a vehicle battery, often used on small engines, is called
questions.explanation: Magneto ignition systems generate their own electricity through a magneto, making them independent of a separate vehicle battery.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A modern ignition system that eliminates the mechanical distributor, using electronic control to fire spark plugs directly, is called
questions.explanation: Distributorless ignition systems (DIS) use electronic control to fire spark plugs directly, removing the need for a mechanical distributor.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The ignition system component that generates the high voltage needed to produce a spark at the spark plug is called the
questions.explanation: The ignition coil steps up the battery's low voltage to the very high voltage needed to jump the spark plug gap and ignite the fuel mixture.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The ignition system component that distributes the high-voltage spark to the correct cylinder at the correct time, in conventional ignition systems, is called the
questions.explanation: In conventional ignition systems, the distributor routes the high-voltage spark to each spark plug in the correct firing order and timing.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The ignition system component that produces the spark inside the combustion chamber to ignite the air-fuel mixture is called the
questions.explanation: The spark plug delivers the electrical spark directly into the combustion chamber, igniting the compressed air-fuel mixture.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The 'heat range' of a spark plug refers to its ability to
options: produce a stronger or weaker spark voltage
dissipate heat from its tip at an appropriate rate for the engine's operating conditions
questions.explanation: Spark plug heat range describes how quickly the plug dissipates heat from its tip, which must suit the engine's typical operating temperature to avoid fouling or pre-ignition.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The high-tension (HT) leads in an ignition system are responsible for
options: carrying the high-voltage current from the coil (or distributor) to the spark plugs
carrying low-voltage current to the starter motor
questions.explanation: HT leads (high-tension cables) carry the high-voltage electrical current needed to fire the spark plugs from the coil or distributor.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A small device connected across the contact breaker points in conventional ignition systems, used to reduce arcing and improve spark quality, is called the
questions.explanation: The condenser (capacitor) absorbs excess voltage across the contact breaker points, reducing arcing and prolonging their working life.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The component that temporarily disconnects engine power from the transmission, allowing smooth gear changes, is called the
questions.explanation: The clutch allows the driver to smoothly engage or disengage the engine's power from the transmission, particularly during gear changes.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A clutch design using a single friction plate and diaphragm spring pressure plate, common in most passenger vehicles, is called a
questions.explanation: The single-plate diaphragm clutch, widely used in passenger cars, uses one friction disc and a diaphragm spring to apply clamping pressure.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A clutch design using several friction discs stacked together, often used in heavy-duty or motorcycle applications, is called a
questions.explanation: Multi-plate clutches use several friction discs to transmit higher torque loads within a more compact space, common in heavy-duty and motorcycle applications.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A clutch mechanism that transmits power using hydraulic fluid rather than direct friction contact is called a
questions.explanation: A fluid coupling transmits power through the movement of hydraulic fluid between rotating impellers, rather than through direct mechanical friction.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A transmission requiring the driver to manually select and engage gears using a clutch pedal and gear lever is called a
questions.explanation: A manual gearbox requires the driver to manually operate the clutch and select gears using a gear lever.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A transmission that automatically selects and changes gears without requiring manual driver input is called an
questions.explanation: An automatic gearbox selects and shifts gears automatically, based on factors like vehicle speed and engine load, without a manual clutch pedal.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The mechanism within a manual gearbox that allows gears of different speeds to mesh smoothly without grinding is called the
questions.explanation: Synchromesh mechanisms match the speeds of gears before they engage, allowing smooth, quiet gear changes without clashing.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The rotating shaft that transmits power from the gearbox to the rear axle (in rear-wheel-drive vehicles) is called the
questions.explanation: The propeller shaft transmits rotational power from the gearbox to the rear axle assembly in rear-wheel-drive vehicles.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A flexible joint used in the drive train to allow the propeller shaft to operate at varying angles as the suspension moves is called a
questions.explanation: Universal joints allow the propeller shaft to transmit power smoothly even as its angle changes with suspension movement.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The final drive component that allows the two driven wheels to rotate at different speeds, especially when cornering, is called the
questions.explanation: The differential allows the inside and outside wheels to rotate at different speeds while cornering, preventing tyre scrubbing and drivetrain strain.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The shafts that transmit power from the differential directly to the driven wheels are called the
questions.explanation: Drive axles (half-shafts) transmit power from the differential to each driven wheel individually.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A suspension component made of thin, curved metal strips stacked together, traditionally used especially in heavier vehicles, is called a
questions.explanation: Leaf springs consist of stacked, curved metal strips, traditionally used to support the weight of heavier vehicles like trucks.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A suspension component made of a helically wound metal rod, compressing and expanding to absorb road shocks, is called a
questions.explanation: Coil springs, common in passenger vehicles, are helically wound metal rods that compress and rebound to absorb road irregularities.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A suspension component consisting of a metal bar that twists to absorb suspension movement is called a
questions.explanation: A torsion bar absorbs suspension forces by twisting along its length, storing and releasing energy as the suspension moves.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A suspension component that dampens (controls) the oscillation of springs after they absorb a bump, preventing excessive bouncing, is called a
questions.explanation: Shock absorbers (dampers) control and reduce the oscillation of springs after a bump, preventing continued bouncing and improving ride control.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An independent front suspension design combining a coil spring and shock absorber into a single strut unit is called a
questions.explanation: The MacPherson strut combines the spring and damper into a single compact unit, widely used in independent front suspension designs.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: An independent suspension design using two triangular arms (upper and lower) to control wheel movement is called a
questions.explanation: Double wishbone suspension uses two triangular control arms to precisely manage wheel movement, often offering superior handling characteristics.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A steering system that uses a toothed bar and pinion gear to convert the steering wheel's rotation into side-to-side wheel movement is called
questions.explanation: Rack and pinion steering converts the rotational motion of the steering wheel into linear motion via a pinion gear meshing with a toothed rack.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A steering system using a worm gear and recirculating ball bearings to reduce steering effort, often found in older or heavier vehicles, is called
questions.explanation: Recirculating ball steering uses ball bearings within a worm gear mechanism to reduce friction and steering effort, common in older and heavier vehicles.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The wheel alignment parameter describing the inward or outward tilt of a wheel when viewed from the front of the vehicle is called
questions.explanation: Camber describes the angle of a wheel's tilt inward or outward when viewed from the front, affecting tyre wear and handling.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The wheel alignment parameter describing the forward or backward tilt of the steering axis when viewed from the side of the vehicle is called
questions.explanation: Caster describes the angle of the steering axis tilt viewed from the side, influencing straight-line stability and steering return.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The wheel alignment condition where the front of the wheels point slightly inward toward each other is called
questions.explanation: Toe-in describes wheels angled slightly inward at the front, a setting that can affect tyre wear and directional stability.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A hydraulic braking system's component that converts pedal pressure into hydraulic pressure sent to the wheel brakes is called the
questions.explanation: The master cylinder converts the driver's foot pressure on the brake pedal into hydraulic pressure, transmitted through brake lines to the wheels.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A type of brake using a friction-lined shoe that presses outward against the inside of a rotating drum is called a
questions.explanation: Drum brakes use curved shoes that press outward against the inner surface of a rotating brake drum to slow the vehicle.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A type of brake using friction pads that clamp onto a rotating metal disc (rotor) is called a
questions.explanation: Disc brakes use a caliper to squeeze friction pads against a rotating disc (rotor), providing effective and consistent stopping power.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The hydraulic component within a drum brake assembly that pushes the brake shoes outward against the drum is called the
questions.explanation: The wheel cylinder, located within the drum brake assembly, uses hydraulic pressure to push the brake shoes outward against the drum.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The classification system used to rate the quality and performance of brake fluid, such as DOT 3 or DOT 4, refers to a standard set by the
questions.explanation: DOT ratings, established by the (US) Department of Transportation, classify brake fluid based on its boiling point and other performance characteristics.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: A braking system technology that prevents the wheels from locking up during hard braking, helping maintain steering control, is called
questions.explanation: ABS modulates brake pressure at each wheel to prevent lock-up during hard braking, helping the driver maintain steering control.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The vehicle electrical circuit responsible for supplying the initial power to crank the engine into operation is called the
questions.explanation: The starting circuit, including the battery, starter motor, and solenoid switch, supplies the power needed to crank the engine to life.

questions.subject: Auto Mechanics
questions.text: The vehicle electrical circuit responsible for recharging the battery and supplying electrical power while the engine is running is called the
questions.explanation: The charging circuit, centred on the alternator and voltage regulator, keeps the battery charged and supplies electrical power once the engine is running.
